alignments.note: Fronted numeral predicate of a verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate rather than the subject (rule 20), and the unit is discontinuous under rule 25.
Construct noun אֹרֶךְ takes only its own word; the phrase's single written *the* belongs to the present article morpheme on the rectum (rule 29).

Article on הַקָּרֶשׁ takes the one *the* the ASV writes for this chain, which English fronts onto the construct while rendering the rectum without an article of its own (rule 29's fronting clause). Competing reading: mark it `unrepresented` — the ASV writes *a board*, so the rectum is rendered indefinitely — and treat *the* as supplied on the construct; rejected because rule 29 supplies a *the* only where no article morpheme is present and marks an article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all.
Nomen rectum with the relational *of*; the indefinite *a* belongs to the noun that licenses it (rules 15, 19).
The indefinite *a* belongs to the noun it determines (rule 15).
Construct חֲצִי rendered *a half*, with the indefinite article belonging to the nominal expression (rule 15).
Article on the second אַמָּה, whose noun the ASV does not render, so nothing is written for it either (rule 29).

The ASV writes *cubit* once, beside the first occurrence, and closes the figure with *half*; this repeated noun is the unrendered occurrence (rule 22). Competing reading: rule 22's tail-to-tail clause would give the English noun to the last occurrence, but that clause governs a counted noun distributed across a compound numeral where the English noun closes the whole English figure, which it does not here.
Construct noun רֹחַב takes only its own word; the second chain's single *the* belongs to the article on its rectum (rule 29).
Article on the rectum, taking the fronted *the* on the same terms as s004; of the phrase's two articles the first takes it (rules 29, 47).
Nomen rectum with the relational *of*; discontinuous around *each* (rules 19, 25).
Agreement article on the numeral; the phrase's one *the* is taken by the first article (rule 47).

review_notes: Corrected on the same point as vv. 9 and 15: the single written *the* of each measurement chain goes to the present article morpheme on the rectum, fronted onto the construct, rather than to a supplied article beside an `unrepresented` present article (rule 29; rule 47 for the second chain's two articles). The first chain's competing reading is named in its note, since the ASV renders that rectum *a board*.
*was* joins the fronted numeral predicate under rule 20: *Ten cubits* is the predicate and *the length of a board* the subject.
חֲצִי הָאַמָּה writes אַמָּה a second time; the ASV's single *cubit* is given to the first occurrence, and the note names the tail-to-tail reading and why rule 22's clause does not reach it.
